queries: "Rethinking Reward Model Evaluation Through the Lens of Reward Overoptimization"

closest.title: Safety Hacking in Constrained Best-of-N Inference-time Scaling
closest.how_close: Very close: sweeps N over frozen-policy responses, filters with Llama Guard or ShieldGemma, reranks with learned rewards, and measures safety failures using HarmBench and a separate rubric-based LLM evaluator. Includes Skywork-Reward-V2 and demonstrates amplification of guard false acceptances. Uses hard safety filtering followed by reward maximization rather than directly maximizing guard safety scores or sweeping LARA penalties.

closest.title: Best-of-N through the Smoothing Lens: KL Divergence and Regret Analysis
closest.how_close: Studies BoN overoptimization and KL scaling, including experiments where independently judged harmlessness deteriorates at large N and smoothing mitigates degradation. Selection uses reward models rather than dedicated safety guards; it does not establish guard-size-dependent safety scaling laws.

closest.title: Rethinking Reward Model Evaluation Through the Lens of Reward Overoptimization
closest.how_close: Connects reward-model evaluation to overoptimization and evaluates BoN safety on WildGuardTest with independent refusal/compliance judgments. Its safety experiment fixes N=16, rather than sweeping guard-selection pressure or fitting safety-overoptimization curves.

rationale: The broad gap is already substantially addressed outside the bibliography. [Safety Hacking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22915) measures how increasing constrained BoN budgets amplifies errors in learned safety guards, using several of the proposed models and benchmarks. However, its selection mechanism is a hard guard threshold followed by reward maximization, which differs materially from increasing optimization pressure directly on guard scores or LARA-augmented rewards. [Smoothing Lens](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05913) also demonstrates independently judged harmlessness degradation under increasing BoN selection pressure, but uses reward proxies. I found no paper combining direct guard-score optimization, N and safety-penalty sweeps, guard-size comparisons, and fitted gold-safety-versus-KL scaling laws with benign over-refusal analysis. These remaining distinctions support a narrow extension, while the central empirical motivation has very close precedents.
